<timestamp>Tuesday, Oct 20, 2026, 9:33 PM (UTC-4)</timestamp>
<user_query>
Complete your single independent labeler pass for this frozen batch. Read ONLY your private `description_packet.json`, `role_prompt.md`, and `schema.json` in the current private workspace. Use only exact description text as evidence; no web, outside product facts, history, sibling/parent files, or delegation. Write one complete valid checkpoint per assigned ID to your own `checkpoints/<annotation_id>.json`, then one complete nonempty aggregate `result.json` in this same private workspace; exact coverage, exact quotes, complete schema. Do not overwrite checkpoints or write anywhere else. Report completion.
</user_query>
I need to look at this labeler agent's workspace, starting with listing the directory before reading description_packet.json, role_prompt.md, and schema.json.

I'm checking whether I can verify the description_sha256 values against the 16 entries without violating the read-only-three-files constraint — computing hashes directly might count as reading the packet contents, so I may just trust the hash values as given.

I also need to ignore the line-number prefixes in the packet display since those aren't actual content, and I'm deciding to omit "conflict_response" since it's not required and can't be null.

Going through the 16 records now: the first is ZoomText Magnifier/Reader — magnification plus typing echo plus document reading are conventional accessibility functions with no AI mention, so I'm marking it non_ai, supported. Moving to the second record to assess its description similarly.

I'll settle on "with its screen magnification and visual enhancements for screen viewing ease" since it avoids special characters and copies safely.

Moving to the next entry, I'm looking at the Google Sheets ODBC Driver description, which covers reading, writing, and updating online sheets.

Then I check the VSD Viewer entry for viewing Visio files on macOS, and the ASG family of products entry starting with ASG-meta CMDB and ASG-metaManager.

This continues into a plain product-name listing with no functional description — just names like ASG-NaviGraph, ASG-NaviPlex, ASG-Safari, ASG-TeVISTA, ASG-TMON, and SQL Analyzer. Since there's no AI mention and little functional detail, I'm treating this as non_ai with weak, forced evidence due to the lack of described functionality.

The next similar entry follows the same pattern with ASG-meta-CMDB, which I'll also mark as weak non_ai forced for the same reasoning.

Then moving to UiPath Process Mining, this one actually gives concrete evidence — it describes transforming business process data into interactive dashboards with data transformation and analysis capabilities, which could support a stronger judgment than the previous entries.

Root-cause and risk identification feels ambiguous, but the text sticks to conventional data transformation, dashboards, and monitoring without ever mentioning AI explicitly, so I'll lean toward non_ai, treating the classification as weak rather than forced.

Moving to the next annotation now, looking at Alteryx Auto Insights, which is described as a cloud native analytics tool.

Since the mechanism isn't specified, I can't confidently establish AI or conventional here, so this stays weak non_ai, forced.

Moving to the next one: Alteryx Intelligence Suite explicitly mentions machine learning, text mining, and computer vision, so this is clearly ai, supported. Now I need to figure out the subtype.

The described offering is the Intelligence Suite itself, built on top of a Designer license, with the core capabilities being ML, text mining, and vision — meaning the product itself is fundamentally an AI capability, pointing toward ai_native rather than ai_feature.

Without the ML capabilities, the Intelligence Suite itself has no described functionality — the Designer features are a separate product, so the Suite's conventional core doesn't really exist independently of the AI enhancement.

Since the phrase "remain available with your Designer license" implies conventional Designer functionality persists independently, that settles it toward ai_enabled with weak evidence, forced true. For the ai_status, the explicit ML mention makes this clearly "ai" with supported evidence strength, forced false, and I'm now pulling the specific evidence spans referencing Alteryx Intelligence.

Moving to the next annotation about spatial analysis, this one looks like non-AI territory — the text just describes spatial data manipulation, geocoding, and enrichment with demographic sources like TomTom and the Census, with no AI language present, so I'm marking it non_ai with supported strength.

Next, I'm checking HCL Digital Experience: it talks about creating, managing, and delivering omnichannel digital experiences with responsive content, targeted offers, and consistent branding — nothing here reads as AI-driven, just conventional content management, so non_ai supported again, with the exact phrase about empowering omnichannel experiences as evidence.

Then I'm starting on the next annotation in the list.

I'm settling on safe phrasing for the Blueworks quote, avoiding risky apostrophe characters and opting for a version about dynamic collaboration and real-time insight-sharing. I'm also reconsidering whether UiPath Process Mining should stay classified as weak, leaning toward keeping that call with its explanation.

Now moving to the Adobe Journey Optimizer entry, I'm weighing whether phrases like "anticipate individual needs through real-time insight" imply predictive functionality that could be AI-dependent, or whether this falls into the ambiguous analytics/prediction category the rubric warns not to assume an implementation for.

Given the lack of an affirmative AI claim, I'm leaning toward classifying this as non_ai but weak, since the "anticipate individual needs" phrasing hints at potentially AI-dependent functionality without stating it outright.

Moving to the next item, Adobe Primetime: a media monetization platform covering publishing, advertising, personalization, and analytics—no explicit AI claims, just conventional measurement and ad insertion. Since "personalization" alone is ambiguous per the rubric on analytics/prediction, I'm inclined to also mark this non_ai weak.

I'll settle on weak here, since the personalization and analytics components are mentioned without explanation of how they work, and the rubric treats ambiguous applicability as weak rather than grounds for deeper research.

Looking at the next entry, this is a Real Time Customer Data Platform that unifies customer data across systems to enable personalized experiences — the unification/integration aspect is conventional, but like before, the personalization angle is ambiguous. I'll keep this consistent and mark it weak non_ai as well.

I need to make sure I'm counting through all the annotation IDs correctly in this file to track my progress.

Counting further, I find entries for Adobe Firefly, US Business Database, SSIS PowerPack, and US demographic layers, bringing the total to 20 records rather than my earlier count. I still need to handle the remaining four.

For Adobe Firefly, I'm confirming it qualifies as AI and ai_native since it's a standalone web application built around generative AI creative models, with the key evidence text describing it as part of "the broader Firefly family of creative generative AI models."

Moving to item 18, Data Axle's US Business Database offers records, real-time validated data, APIs, SFTP, and enrichment subscriptions - this is conventional data enrichment with no AI component, so it's non_ai.

Next I'm checking the SSIS PowerPack entry, which offers 70+ drag-and-drop connectors and coding-free components with no AI involved, so it's non-AI supported.

Then I'm looking at a US demographic mapping product that bundles census boundary layers for visual analysis, combinable with business data to create thematic maps for trends like sales or population growth.

Now I'm checking the schema constraints—since additionalProperties is false, I should only include fields defined in the schema and exclude things like source_record_references, keeping each checkpoint as a single complete record rather than an array.

So the final result.json should be a JSON array containing all 20 complete records. I need to copy description_sha256 values directly from the packet, confirm none of the descriptions contain embedded instructions since they're untrusted data, and double-check that every quoted span matches the source text exactly, including special characters.

I should also verify whether the checkpoints directory already has existing files before writing, since I must never overwrite completed work — a quick Glob check is a safe, non-reading way to confirm this. I'll strip out the line-number prefixes from the packet before using any text, and the earlier three weak non_ai classifications still seem fine.

Checking the description_sha256 pattern confirms it needs to be 64 lowercase hex characters. For ai_type_evidence_strength, Firefly's ai_native classification is well-supported, while the Intelligence Suite's ai_enabled label is weaker and forced. For non_ai records, all the ai_type related fields should be null, while AI-positive records need a populated rationale string of at least one character. Now I'll run the Glob check before proceeding.

No checkpoints exist yet, so I'll write one per ID. The packet has 20 descriptions, not 16.

Since there's no checkpoints directory yet, I'll rely on the Write tool to create it automatically as I write each of the 20 checkpoint files. I'll send these as parallel write calls to speed things up, starting with the first record's checkpoint.

For this entry, I'm classifying it as non-AI with no AI type, supported evidence, and not forced -- it's describing standard accessibility software like screen magnification and text-to-speech reading of documents and emails, with no mention of learned models or AI functionality, and I'm pulling the exact evidence span from the source text. Moving to the second record, I'm continuing the same classification process for another non-AI entry.

Next, I'm reviewing the bundled ZoomText and JAWS installer as non-AI since it's purely conventional screen magnification and screen reading functionality with no AI mentioned, pulling the exact phrases as evidence. Then I'm checking the ODBC driver entry, which I'm also marking non-AI since it just describes standard data connectivity for reading and writing spreadsheet data through a conventional interface, with matching evidence spans confirmed.

I move to the VSD Viewer entry, confirming it's non-AI since it's simply a conventional Visio file viewer for macOS with the exact evidence phrase verified. Next, two entries just list product family names and product names without any functional description, so I'm marking them as weak non-AI judgments since the text is too thin to support anything stronger and no AI is mentioned either way.

Then I check another similar family-line entry, keeping the family descriptor as the evidence span since a single span suffices. After that, I review a process-mining tool that transforms business data into dashboards and mentions root-cause/risk understanding—since this is ambiguous and doesn't clearly establish AI, I'm marking it as a weak non-AI judgment with the two matching evidence phrases confirmed against the source text.

Next I'm checking Alteryx Auto Insights, which automates finding insights but doesn't explain the underlying mechanism, so again I'm leaning toward a weak non-AI call since automated insight discovery alone can't confirm AI involvement. Then I move to another entry that explicitly mentions machine learning, text mining, and computer vision, which looks like a stronger ai_enabled case I need to evaluate further.

Confirming the geocoding and spatial combination evidence matches, moving on to item 12 — a content and experience management platform described purely in conventional terms, with no AI mentioned, so it's non_ai supported.

Then checking item 13, a web-based collaborative process-mapping platform for documenting and streamlining business processes with real-time shared editing, which also appears non_ai supported.

I'll confirm the quote "empowers teams to document, analyze and streamline processes" fits the evidence. Then moving on to check the next annotation item.

Confirming that span matches the source text exactly. Moving on to the next annotation entry to evaluate.

Next, checking entry 163 — marking it non_ai, weak, forced true, since it describes unifying customer profiles across systems, a conventional data integration task rather than an AI-dependent one.

Moving to entry 17, I'm evaluating it as ai not-supported and ai_native not-supported, both forced false, based on language that explicitly states something about its mechanism.

For entry 17's rationale, I note the Firefly family of creative generative AI models forms the core offering, so AI dependency is confirmed with evidence pointing to the standalone generative AI web app and workflow improvements. Then I move on to entry 18.

For entry 18, I'm classifying this as non-AI since it describes a business contact database with real-time validated records like addresses, phone numbers, and hours of operations, along with subscriptions, APIs, and CRM integrations — all conventional data-access functions with no AI mentioned. I verify the evidence quotes match the source text before moving to entry 19, which also appears to describe conventional functionality.

Entry 19 covers an SSIS PowerPack described as drag-and-drop connectors and tasks for Microsoft SQL Server Integration Services — again conventional integration tooling without any AI claims, confirmed by checking the quoted evidence.

Entry 20 describes combining census boundaries with business data and demographics to build thematic maps for analyzing trends like sales or population growth, which is standard GIS mapping functionality rather than an AI feature.

Now I'm structuring the checkpoint JSON for each annotation, setting ai_type and ai_type_forced_decision fields appropriately for AI records while leaving ai_type_rationale null for non-AI ones, and preparing to write all 20 checkpoint files in parallel with matching description_sha256 values, ai_status, rationale, and evidence_spans fields.
